Indicators.Name: Account lockout duration below recommended threshold
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether the account lockout duration is configured to less than 60 seconds. A short lockout duration may increase the risk of successful brute-force attacks and is not aligned with Microsoft Entra security best practices.

Required permissions

  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
To remediate this issue, increase the account lockout duration to at least 60 seconds:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link) as a Global Administrator, Security Administrator, or Authentication Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Protection > Authentication methods > Password protection.
  3. Under Lockout duration in seconds, set the value to 60 or higher.
  4. Click Save to apply the changes.

Note: Be cautious when setting this value. While a longer lockout duration enhances security, it can also impact user experience and potentially increase support calls for account unlocks.

Indicators.Name: Account lockout threshold below recommended minimum
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether the account lockout threshold is configured to fewer than 10 failed sign-in attempts. A low threshold may lead to user lockouts from accidental sign-in failures while offering limited additional protection against brute-force attacks.

Required permissions

  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
To remediate this issue, increase the account lockout threshold to at least 10 failed attempts:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link) as a Global Administrator, Security Administrator, or Authentication Administrator.
  2. Navigate to Protection > Authentication methods > Password protection.
  3. Under Lockout threshold, set the Number of failed authentication attempts allowed to 10 or higher.
  4. Click Save to apply the changes.

Note: Be cautious when setting this value. While a higher threshold enhances security, it should be balanced with user experience considerations.

Indicators.Name: Application instance property lock disabled
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for applications that have app instance property lock disabled.

Required permissions

  • Application.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enable the application instance lock feature and all of its properties for app registrations.

To enable the instance property lock of an application, Sign in to Microsoft Entra admin center as at least a Cloud Application Administrator. In the Applications tab, click on App Registrations and select the application to be configured. Select Authentication, and then select Configure under the App instance property lock section. In the App instance property lock pane, enter the settings for the lock.

Indicators.Name: User consent is allowed for risky applications
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for an Entra ID authorization policy that allows users to grant consent for risky applications.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enable risk-based step-up consent in Entra ID.

The configuration for enabling risk-based step-up consent is not exposed in the Entra admin center, and must be configured either through PowerShell or the Graph API.

Indicators.Name: Application name and geographic location additional contexts are disabled on MFA
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if the Microsoft Authenticator App settings are configured to display the name of the target application and geographical location of the request when a user receives a push notification.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enable Show application name in push and passwordless notifications and Show geographic location in push and passwordless notifications in Entra ID.

The configuration for additional context settings passwords can be found in Authentication methods - Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link).

To browse to the settings in the Microsoft Entra admin center, expand the Protection menu on the left, select Authentication methods, and then Policies. Once in Authentication methods, select Microsoft Authenticator on the right blade. The Microsoft Authenticator settings blade will open, and from the top menu select Configure. In the list of settings the status for Show application name in push and passwordless notifications and Show geographic location in push and passwordless notifications should both be changed to Enabled. The Target for the settings should be Include and set to All users.

Indicators.Name: Conditional Access policy with Continuous Access Evaluation disabled
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for Conditional Access policies that have Continuous Access Evaluation disabled.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enable Continuous Access Evaluation on the indicated Conditional Access policies in Entra ID.

To enable, browse to the impacted policies in the Conditional Access blade, Conditional Access - Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link).

To browse to the settings in the Microsoft Entra admin center, expand the Protection menu on the left, select Conditional Access. On the right you will want to select Policies and find the impacted policies in the list. Select the policy, which will open the settings for it. Under Access controls select the Session setting. In the window that opens on the right, uncheck the box for Customize continuous access evaluation.

Indicators.Name: Certificate-based authentication persistence exposure
Indicators.Description:
This indicator looks for the presence of specific Entra ID Microsoft Graph app roles and permissions that, when combined, can enable a principal to establish persistence through certificate-based authentication (CBA).

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • RoleManagement.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
  • Application.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
To mitigate the risk associated with Certificate-based authentication (CBA) persistence, it is recommended that the organization review and evaluate the necessity of the permissions and role assignments that can be leveraged for a CBA attack.

Limit the assignment of the following permissions only to trusted apps that need the ability to add a Root CA if CBA is enabled:

  • Authentication Policy Administrator
  • Application with Policy.ReadWrite.AuthenticationMethod and Organization.ReadWrite.All permissions

Remove the following roles and permissions from any account that does not require them for operational purposes:

  • Privileged Role Administrator
  • Privileged Authentication Administrator
  • RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory
  • AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All

Indicators.Name: Administrative units are not being used
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for the use of administrative units in the Entra tenant.

Required permissions

  • AdministrativeUnit.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the organizational structure and current role assignments, and consider leveraging administrative units to limit privileged user scope.

Like organizational units in Active Directory, administrative unit design and implementation will be specific to the organizations structure.

Administrative units can be configured in the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link). They are located by expanding Identity, expanding Roles & admins and selecting Admin units.

Indicators.Name: Conditional Access policy contains private IP address
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if any named locations contains private IP addresses and are assigned to enabled Conditional Access policies.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the impacted Conditional Access policy, and verify the policy conditions are working as expected.

If the policy is working as expected, the Named location should be removed from the policy, as private IP addresses or ranges are not used in Conditional Access evaluation.

If the policy is not working as expected and is designed to evaluate based on network location, the Named location should be changed to reflect the egress IP addresses or ranges.

Organizations must ensure that all Conditional Access policy changes are documented and verify that they do not cause unintended negative impact

Named locations can be reviewed in the Entra admin center (direct link). To browse to them, on the left menu, expand Protection and then expand Conditional Access. In the blade on the right, select Named locations.

Indicators.Name: Guest user with permission to invite other guests
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for guest users that have permission to invite other guests.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Change guest invite restrictions from the setting Anyone in the organization can invite guest users including guests and non-admins (most-inclusive) in the Entra tenant.

To change, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand External Identities, and select External collaboration settings.

In the blade on the right, change the radio dial selection under Guest invite settings, Guest invite restrictions.

Organizations need to make a determination on what guest invite restriction setting to select, as they have different levels of restrictions on both users and guests. Ensure that any changes are communicated out, as they can impact existing business processes.

Select Save at the top of the blade.

Indicators.Name: User or device inactive for over 90 days
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for users or devices that have not signed in to Entra ID in the past 90 days.

Required permissions

  • Device.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Evaluate the indicated inactive users and devices for management as per your organizational policy.

If the organization does not have a policy defining account management, NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 covers account lifecycle controls under AC-2 (3).

Indicated user objects can be found under the Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Users, and select All users. You can search for the impacted users in the right blade.

Indicated user objects can be found under the Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Devices, and select All devices. You can search for the impacted users in the right blade.

Indicators.Name: Legacy authentication is allowed
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if legacy authentication is blocked either by Conditional Access policies or Security Defaults.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Create a Conditional Access policy blocking legacy authentication.

Microsoft provides both a Conditional Access policy template, as well as step-by-step instructions for creating a Conditional Access policy to block legacy authentication.

If legacy authentication is still required for limited resources that may utilize it, such as SMTP with Exchange Online, additional Conditional Access policies should be created for those resources to limit authentication to trusted IP ranges.

Creation and deployment of Conditional Access policies can negatively impact users if not tested. Organizations need to ensure that policies are tested before broad deployment.

Indicators.Name: Conditional Access policy that contains MFA Trusted IP
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if any enabled Conditional Access policies contain references to MFA Trusted IPs.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
IP addresses and ranges in Multifactor authentication trusted IPs should be creates as a Named location to be used by the impacted Conditional Access policies.

To configure, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Protection, expand Conditional Access, and select Named locations.

To view existing trusted IPs, select the Configure multifactor authentication trusted IPs (direct link) link on the upper portion of the right blade, then click on Service settings. A new named location should be created containing the same ranges.

Creation and deployment of Conditional Access policies can negatively impact users if not tested. Organizations need to ensure that policies are tested before broad deployment.

Organizations that are using AD FS with Entra Multifactor authentication, per-user MFA, or Entra MFA server may need to retain their trusted IP settings.

Indicators.Name: Privileged group contains guest account
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether any privileged roles have been assigned to guest accounts.

Required permissions

  • User.Read.All
  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the guest users identified and their assigned roles in the Entra tenant, and determine if they should continue to hold these unused roles. The organization should fully understand the associated risk involved with the guest holding the role assignment. A privileged access strategy should follow a governance plan for assigning least privilege, such as that documented in NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5.

You can review existing role assignments in the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link).

Organizations should use the Access Reviews feature of Entra Privileged Identity Management to help manage the lifecycle of privileged role assignments.

Indicators.Name: Privileged account with no MFA
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks that MFA (Multi-factor Authentication) is enabled for users assigned privileged roles.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Users identified as impacted must be configured to require MFA at minimum for authentication in Entra ID.

Break-glass accounts may be an exception to MFA requirements, and can be added to an ignore list for this indicator. Organizations need to monitor their break-glass accounts to ensure that the accounts are not used without awareness

Microsoft provides both a Conditional Access policy template, as well as step-by-step instructions for creating a Conditional Access Policy requiring MFA for administrators. If a Conditional Access policy already exists for privileged users, the identified users can be added to that policy.

Organizations that do not have licensing for Conditional Access policies should enable Security Defaults.

Indicators.Name: Application service principal with risky API permission
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if one of the following risky application permissions have been granted to a service principal in Microsoft Graph: RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory, AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All

Required permissions

  • Application.Read.All
  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Before removing the permissions, investigate the application's activity to determine if the high-risk permissions are actively required for legitimate business operations. Review the Microsoft Entra audit logs for any recent, unexpected role assignments or directory modifications performed by the service principal, as this could indicate an active compromise.

Caution: Removing consented application permissions may result in degraded or broken functionality of the application. Organizations must verify the application's true operational needs before revoking access.

To review and revoke permissions for the affected application:

  1. Open the Microsoft Entra admin center .
  2. Expand Identity , expand Applications , and select Enterprise applications .
  3. Search for the affected application by name and select it.
  4. In the left navigation menu, under Security , select Permissions .
  5. Review the assigned permissions shown on the page. To revoke application permissions, select Review permissions in the top menu.

Indicators.Name: User with weak or no MFA
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks all users for their registered MFA types.

Required permissions

  • AuditLog.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Examine the feasibility of requiring users to use a strong form of MFA.

The Authentication methods activity report in Entra ID can provide usage details on MFA methods for users in the Entra tenant.

To view, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Show more, expand Monitoring & health, select Usage & insights. In the right blade, select Authentication methods activity.

Users may have weaker forms of MFA registered, but are not actively using them, and should be evaluated to remove them. A registration campaign can help users in the organization enroll in the Microsoft Authenticator App for MFA.

To configure a registration campaign, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Protection, select Authentication methods. In the right blade, select Registration campaign.

Organizations need to understand the risk of users not having MFA enabled on their accounts. If MFA is not feasible, organizations should determine if other compensating controls can be put in place, such as network or device compliance restrictions through Conditional Access policies.

Indicators.Name: Security defaults not enabled
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether security defaults are enabled when there are no Conditional Access policies configured.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enable security defaults or Conditional Access policies.

If the organization is licensed for Entra ID P1 or higher, or associated EMS or M365 licensing, it is preferred to use Conditional Access for securing authentication.

If the licensing is not available, then an organization should enable security defaults.

To enable, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Users, and select Overview.

In the blade on the right, select Properties. Under the Security defaults section towards the bottom, select Manage security defaults. Set Security defaults to Enabled. Select Save.

If Conditional Access is currently used by the organization, it should not enable Security defaults.

Indicators.Name: Non-synced Entra user eligible for a privileged role
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for Entra users that are eligible for a high-privilege role and have the proxyAddress attribute, but are not synchronized with an AD account.

Required permissions:

  • User.Read.All
  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • Directory.Read.All
  • Organization.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Ensure that the users indicated in the results are configured for MFA, which will prevent the ability for an attacker to authenticate as the compromised user in Entra ID, even if the attacker attempts SMTP matching abuse.

Further, organizations can disable soft-matching in their Entra tenant to protect against this takeover. Disabling soft-matching should not be a replacement for enablement of MFA on privileged users in Entra ID.

Full details on the attack, detection and preventative remediation can be found in the referenced Semperis article.

Indicators.Name: Unrestricted user consent allowed
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if users are allowed to add applications from unverified publishers to Entra ID.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Do not allow users to consent to applications from unverified publishers.

To disable consent for all applications, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Applications, and select Enterprise applications.

In the blade on the right, under Security select Consent and permissions. In the new blade that opens, under User consent settings ensure that Allow user consent for apps is not selected.

Organizations must understand that changes they make to the application consent process can impact users onboarding new applications, and the organizations must communicate out the changes as needed to impacted users.

Indicators.Name: Custom banned password protection not in use
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if custom banned password protection is enabled in Entra ID.

Required permissions

  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enable Enforce custom list in Entra ID and populate the Custom banned password list.

To enable, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Protection and select Authentication methods.

In the blade on the right, select Password protection.

Set Enforce custom list to Enabled if it is not already enabled.

Enter custom banned words.

Organizations should also routinely verify the list and make additions or changes as needed.

Indicators.Name: Non-privileged principal assigned high-risk custom role
Indicators.Description:
This indicator identifies non-privileged principals that are assigned custom Entra ID directory roles containing sensitive permissions, scoped to a specific application (service principal). Examples of flagged permissions include the ability to:

  • Create or delete applications
  • Modify application or service principal properties
  • Update application or service principal credentials
  • Modify application ownership or permissions
  • Update directory policies or group properties
  • Read BitLocker recovery keys

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • Directory.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
  • GroupMember.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Before removing the role assignments, investigate the activity of the identified non-privileged principals by reviewing the Microsoft Entra sign-in and audit logs. This helps determine if they are actively using the high-risk permissions for legitimate business operations or if the assignment was a misconfiguration.

Caution: Removing custom role assignments might disrupt legitimate administrative workflows or break automation scripts and applications that rely on these permissions. Verify the necessity of the access before revoking it.

To review and remove the risky role assignments:

  1. Open the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Expand Identity, expand Roles & admins, and select Roles & admins.
  3. Search for the custom role in question and select it.
  4. In the left navigation menu, select Assignments.
  5. Review the assigned principals. Select the checkbox next to any non-privileged principals that should not have this access, and select Remove assignment.

Indicators.Name: Conditional Access policy disabling admin token persistence
Indicators.Description:
This indicator looks for Conditional Access policies that disable token persistence for users who have admin roles and a sign-in frequency of 9 hours or less.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Deploy a Conditional Access policy that enforces sign-in frequency for privileged users.

To create a Conditional Access policy, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Protection and select Conditional Access.

In the blade on the right, select Policies. Select New Policy. A new policy should be created that is scoped to the following privileged roles with a time interval of 9 hours or less:

Agent ID Administrator, AI Administrator, AI Reader, Application Administrator, Application Developer, Attribute Provisioning Administrator, Attribute Provisioning Reader, Authentication Administrator, Authentication Extensibility Administrator, Authentication Extensibility Password Administrator, Authentication Policy Administrator, B2C IEF Keyset Administrator, Billing Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator, Cloud Device Administrator, Conditional Access Administrator, Directory Synchronization Accounts, Directory Writers, Domain Name Administrator, Exchange Administrator, External Identity Provider Administrator, Global Administrator, Global Reader, Helpdesk Administrator, Hybrid Identity Administrator, Identity Governance Administrator, Intune Administrator, Lifecycle Workflows Administrator, Partner Tier1 Support, Partner Tier2 Support, Password Administrator, Privileged Authentication Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, Security Administrator, Security Operator, Security Reader, SharePoint Administrator, User Administrator.

Conditional Access policies can negatively impact user authentication, and organizations must verify their policies before deployment.

Indicators.Name: Dynamic administrative unit with self-assignment risk
Indicators.Description:
This indicator detects cases where a user assigned to manage a dynamic administrative unit (AU) also has permissions to modify the attribute(s) used to determine AU membership. Entra ID supports dynamic AUs, where user membership is automatically determined by property-based rules (e.g., department, job title). If misconfigured, this setup can be abused to bypass scoping restrictions and escalate privileges.

Required permissions

  • AdministrativeUnit.Read.All
  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • User.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Organizations should review the configuration of dynamic administrative units (AUs) to ensure that attribute-based membership rules cannot be influenced by users who have administrative roles over the AU.

Start by identifying AUs with dynamic membership rules and cross-reference the attributes used for membership with the permissions of AU administrators. If any administrators can modify the properties that determine AU membership, this access should be revoked or scoped appropriately.

Ensure that AUs are used as intended - to segment administrative duties, and that dynamic membership logic does not create opportunities for privilege escalation. If possible, redesign AU logic to use attributes that cannot be modified by scoped admins.

  1. To review administrative units, open the Microsoft Entra admin center
  2. Expand Roles & admins.
  3. Select Admin units.
  4. Review each AU by clicking on it.
  5. Check the Dynamic membership rules to see which rules are affecting the AU.

Indicators.Name: Application with expired secret or certificate
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for certificates or secrets that have reached their expiration date. It does not indicate a direct risk or likelihood of compromise.

Required permissions

  • Application.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Remove the expired credentials from the indicated applications in Entra ID. Expired credentials are not useable in Entra ID.

To remove, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Applications, and select App registrations.

In the blade on the right, search for the indicated app registrations. Note that you might need to select All applications to search.

Select the impacted app registration name, which will open a new blade. In this blade, under Manage select Certificates & secrets.

You will need to select Certificates or Client secrets depending on the type of expired credential. In the list you'll see the expired credential marked with a red warning indicator. Verify that the credential is the correct expired one to delete, and select the trash can on the right.

Deleting actively used, non-expired credentials will have negative impact on the applications using them.

Note: If the service principal ID is N/A, no matching service principal exists in this tenant for the specified application ID (for example, the app hasn't been consented in this tenant, or removed).

Indicators.Name: FIDO2 Attestation not enforced
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if FIDO2 security key attestation is enforced in Entra ID.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enable Enforce attestation in Entra ID for FIDO2 security key settings.

To enable, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Protection and select Authentication methods.

In the blade on the right, select Policies, and then under Method select FIDO2 security key.

In the new blade that opens, select Configure from the top menu. Toggle Enforce attestation to yes.

Select Save at the bottom of the blade.

Organizations must test changes to FIDO2 security key settings as this change is user impacting to enrollments, and ensure that changes are communicated out as necessary

Indicators.Name: Entra Connect Sync account password reset
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if there have been any password resets against Entra Connect Sync Sync_ accounts not logged on in the past three days, which are considered stale.

Required permissions

  • AuditLog.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the accounts listed in the results of this indicator.

If the Entra Connect server was offline for known reasons and the password was recently changed by the organization running a password rotation on the account, then this result might be expected.

If the account listed is associated with a no longer used Entra Connect server, it should be deleted from Entra ID.

If this account is believed to be suspicious, the Audit logs for the account activity can be viewed in Entra ID.

To view the audit logs, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Users, and select All users.

In the blade on the right, search for the user indicated in the results. Select the user account.

In the user blade that opens, select Audit logs. The audit log details of changes made will be shown.

If the account is believed to be compromised, organizations must perform a thorough audit analysis of the user account

Removing an active Entra Connect synchronization user account will break synchronization

Indicators.Name: Global Administrator signed in during the last 14 days
Indicators.Description:
This indicator looks for Global Administrators that have signed in during the past 14 days.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the Global Administrators listed in the results of this indicator.

If an organization believes that there is highly suspicious activity or a confirmed compromise of a Global Administrator, they must treat this as a critical security event.

If this account is believed to be suspicious, the Audit logs for the account activity can be viewed in Entra ID.

To view the audit logs, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Users, and select All users.

In the blade on the right, search for the user indicated in the results. Select the user account.

In the user blade that opens, select Audit logs. The audit log details of changes made by the user will be shown.

Indicators.Name: Hybrid-synced Global Administrator account
Indicators.Description:
This indicator detects Global Administrator accounts that are synchronized from on-premises Active Directory. According to Microsoft's security guidance, Global Administrator accounts should be cloud-only to minimize exposure and prevent compromise through on-premises infrastructure.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • Directory.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
To mitigate this issue, transition Global Administrator privileges from hybrid-synced accounts to cloud-only accounts:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Create new cloud-only accounts for each administrator:
    • Go to Identity > Users > All users > + New user > Create new user
    • Use a unique naming convention to differentiate from on-premises accounts
    • Assign strong authentication methods and appropriate licenses
  3. Assign the Global Administrator role to the new accounts:
    • Navigate to the user profile > Assigned roles
    • Select + Add assignments and choose "Global Administrator"
  4. Once cloud-only accounts are fully operational, remove Global Administrator rights from the hybrid accounts:
    • Go to Identity > Roles and administrators > Global Administrator
    • Select each hybrid account and remove its role assignment

Note: Maintain at least two cloud-only Global Administrator accounts for emergency access. Protect them with strong authentication and regularly review their configuration and usage.

Indicators.Name: Guest users not restricted
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if guest users are restricted in the Entra tenant.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Change guest user access restrictions to Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive).

To change, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand External Identities, and select External collaboration settings.

In the blade on the right, change the radio dial selection under Guest user access restrictions to Guest user access is restricted to properties and memberships of their own directory objects (most restrictive). Select Save at the top of the blade.

Organizations should understand that this will change behavior for guest users in the Entra tenant, and that the changes should be verified and tested, as well as communicated out to impacted users as needed.

Indicators.Name: Hidden administrative units
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for administrative units that are part of the tenant and have hidden membership enabled. This configuration can allow attackers to hide backdoor identities from all but a handful of privileged roles, increasing the risk of undetected privilege escalation.

Required permissions

  • AdministrativeUnit.Read.All
  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
Indicators.Remediation:
Organizations should regularly audit their hidden administrative units (AUs) in Entra ID to ensure they are not being misused or forgotten. Because hidden AUs cannot be created or viewed via the Entra ID portal, they must be identified and reviewed using Microsoft Graph API or PowerShell. To view the members of hidden AUs, high-privilege roles such as Global Administrator, Privileged Authentication Administrator, or User Administrator are typically required.

Begin by listing all hidden AUs in the tenant and confirming their intended purpose, member objects, and any scoped role assignments. Verify that only authorized and trusted accounts have administrative access to each hidden AU. Remove unnecessary or outdated role assignments. If a hidden AU no longer serves a valid operational or compliance need, consider deleting it to reduce potential attack surface.

Note that once created, an administrative unit cannot be converted back to an unhidden state.

  1. To review hidden administrative units, open the Microsoft Entra admin center using high privilege role such as Global Administrator.
  2. Expand Roles & admins.
  3. Select Admin units.
  4. Review each AU by clicking on it.

Indicators.Name: Hidden and restricted administrative units
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for administrative units in the tenant that have both hidden membership and restricted management enabled. This combination can obscure privileged access, conceal backdoor accounts, and limit visibility to only a few high-privilege roles, making timely detection and remediation more difficult.

Required permissions

  • AdministrativeUnit.Read.All
  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
Indicators.Remediation:
Organizations should prioritize the review of administrative units (AUs) that are both hidden and restricted, as they present a higher risk of undetected misuse. These AUs cannot be created or viewed through the standard Entra ID portal and must be audited using Microsoft Graph or PowerShell. To view the members of hidden AUs, high-privilege roles such as Global Administrator, Privileged Authentication Administrator, or User Administrator are typically required.

Begin by listing all hidden and restricted AUs in the tenant and confirming their intended purpose, member objects, and any scoped role assignments. Verify that only authorized and trusted accounts have administrative access to each AU. Remove unnecessary or outdated role assignments.

If an AU no longer serves a valid operational or compliance need, consider deleting it to reduce potential attack surface. Otherwise, implement strict monitoring, documentation, and periodic audits to ensure its configuration aligns with your organization's access control policies.

Note that once created, an administrative unit cannot be converted back to an unhidden or unrestricted state.

  1. To review hidden and restricted administrative units, open the Microsoft Entra admin center using high privilege role such as Global Administrator.
  2. Expand Roles & admins.
  3. Select Admin units.
  4. Review each AU by clicking on it.

Indicators.Name: Entra tenant is susceptible to Hidden Consent Grant attack
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks app permissions and settings to determine if the Entra tenant is susceptible to Hidden Consent Grant attacks.

Required permissions

  • Directory.Read.All
  • Policy.Read.All
  • Application.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review apps with AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All, DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All or Directory.ReadWrite.All application permissions and remove any unnecessary app privileges. Monitor and revoke any unauthorized OAuth consent grants.

In addition, consider disabling the Users can register applications setting in the Entra tenant, which is enabled by default.

To disable this settings:

Open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Users, and select User settings.

In the blade on the right, toggle Users can register applications to no.

Select Save at the bottom of the blade.

Organizations should understand how this change impacts their users and communicate the change out according to defined business processes.

Indicators.Name: Guest account inactive over 30 days
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for Guest accounts that have not signed in, using an interactive or non-interactive sign in, in the past 30 days.

Required permissions

  • User.Read.All
  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the guest users indicated in the results, and determine if the guest objects should be deleted from Entra ID. If the guest object needs to be kept for infrequent use, the object can alternatively be disabled, and then re-enabled when the guest needs access again.

If licensed for Entra Identity Governance, organizations can leverage inactive guest insights and configure multi-stage guest reviews in Identity Governance, building a robust lifecycle around guest user objects.

To review guest users, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Users, and select All users.

In the blade on the right, search for the guest object identified. Select the guest user. In the user properties, select Delete towards the top on the right blade to delete the user.

If you want to disable the user, under Account status, select Edit, and in the new blade that opens uncheck Account enabled. Select Save at the bottom.

Deleting active guest users objects in Entra ID will negatively impact the users ability to access resources.

Indicators.Name: Less than 2 Global Administrators exist
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for the presence of less than 2 Global Administrators.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • RoleManagement.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Create more than one Global Administrator.

To review and manage role assignments, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, select Show more, expand Roles & admins, and select Roles & admins.

In the blade on the right, find the Global Administrator role. Select the role.

From this view you can add/remove users as necessary from the role. Organizations that have Entra ID P2 licensing available should use access reviews to manage the lifecycle of privileged users.

Organizations must ensure that any addition/removal of the Global Administrator role does not impact the ability to manage their Entra tenant.

Indicators.Name: MFA bombing attack occurred in the past day
Indicators.Description:
This indicator detects MFA bombing attempts on privileged accounts by monitoring login activity to identify unusual patterns of login activity of more than 5 failed MFA attempts within the last day. Note that this indicator will not detect activity of users using passwordless authentication.

Required permissions

  • AuditLog.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
  • RoleManagement.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
To mitigate the risk of MFA bombing attacks, consider implementing the following measures:

  1. Reset the MFA method for the affected accounts.
  2. Set up MFA challenge policies that require users to complete additional authentication steps (e.g. answering security questions, entering a code sent to their phone) after a certain number of login failures.
  3. Increase the rate limiting on MFA attempts. This will make it harder for an attacker to brute force MFA codes.
  4. Use a hardware token for MFA. Hardware tokens are more secure than SMS or phone call-based MFA, as they cannot be easily intercepted or spoofed.
  5. Use a trusted IP range for MFA. If you have a specific range of IP addresses that you trust (e.g. your office location), you can configure MFA to only be required when logging in from outside of that range.
Note: It is important to carefully consider the potential impact of these changes on your users before implementing them. Some of these measures may be more effective at preventing MFA bombing attacks, but they may also be more inconvenient for your users.

Indicators.Name: MFA policy changes for groups and users
Indicators.Description:
This indicator looks for changes (removal of users and groups) from MFA policies. It relates to events invoked more than 4 hours after the policy's creation.

Required permissions

  • AuditLog.Read.All
  • Policy.Read.All
  • GroupMember.Read.All
  • Reports.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation: Review the changes in the MFA policy in the audit log (with the Category of Policy and activity of "Update policy") and make sure they were made by a valid user.

Indicators.Name: More than 10 privileged administrators exist
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for the presence of 10 or more privileged roles assigned.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • RoleManagement.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the users assigned the selected privileged role, and determine if the role assignment can be removed.

To review and manage role assignments, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, select Show more, expand Roles & admins, and select Roles & admins.

In the blade on the right, find the privileged roles role. Select each privileged role.

From this view you can remove users as necessary from the role. Organizations that have Entra ID P2 licensing available should use access reviews to manage the lifecycle of privileged users.

Organizations must ensure that any removal of the privileged role assignment does not impact the ability to manage their Entra tenant.

Indicators.Name: More than 5 Global Administrators exist
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for the presence of 5 or more Global Administrators. Please note: If a given user has both an active and eligible assignment for a given role, the user will appear twice in the results.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • RoleManagement.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the users assigned the Global Administrator role, and determine if the role assignment can be removed.


To review and manage role assignments, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, select Show more, expand Roles & admins, and select Roles & admins.

In the blade on the right, find the Global Administrator role. Select the role.

From this view you can remove users as necessary from the role. Organizations that have Entra ID P2 licensing available should use access reviews to manage the lifecycle of privileged users.

Organizations must ensure that any removal of the Global Administrator role does not impact the ability to manage their Entra tenant.

Indicators.Name: Suspicious root CA added to tenant
Indicators.Description:
This indicator triggers when a new root CA certificate is uploaded to an Entra tenant.

Required permissions

  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
View the data returned by the indicator and verify if new root CA certificates have been added as part of planned maintenance. If the addition of root CA certificates was unplanned, examine the relevant audit log for further details on the suspected principal.

If compromise has been determined, remove the added certificates and follow DFIR protocols to investigate and mitigate other malicious actions performed in the tenant.

Indicators.Name: Password hash synchronization not enabled
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether password hash synchronization is enabled in the tenant.

Required permissions

    OnPremDirectorySynchronization.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enable password hash synchronization in the Entra tenant.

When dealing with password hash synchronization, organizations have options to migrate from pass-through authentication (PTA) or federated authentication, or alternatively organizations can enable password hash synchronization and still leave the authentication method of PTA or federated in place.

Organizations enabling password hash synchronization must ensure they are not changing the authentication method without proper planning and testing.

Depending on whether the organization is looking to migrate from PTA or federated authentication, or if they are looking to enable password hash synchronization without changing authentication, the means of making this change are different in Entra connect.

Indicators.Name: Permanently active privileged role assignment
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for the presence of permanent active privileged role assignments.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • Directory.Read.All
  • Application.Read.All
  • GroupMember.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Limit the duration of activity for privileged roles in PIM to a reasonable timeframe (e.g., up to 90 days) based on the user's role and necessity.

To configure activity durations, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Identity governance, and select Privileged Identity Management.

In the blade on the right, select the specific privileged role you wish to configure. Adjust the activity settings to ensure they are time-bound.

Conduct regular reviews of all privileged roles to ensure that only necessary users have active access, and that this access is appropriately time-bound.

Educate administrators and users about the risks of permanently active roles and the importance of maintaining strict access controls.

Indicators.Name: Hybrid-synced privileged role account
Indicators.Description:
This indicator detects privileged role accounts (excluding Global Administrators) that are synchronized from on-premises Active Directory. According to Microsoft's security guidance, privileged role accounts should be cloud-only to minimize exposure and prevent compromise through on-premises infrastructure.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • Directory.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
To mitigate this issue, transition privileged role permissions from hybrid-synced accounts to cloud-only accounts:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Create new cloud-only accounts for each administrator:
    • Go to Identity > Users > All users > + New user > Create new user
    • Use a unique naming convention to differentiate from on-premises accounts
    • Assign strong authentication methods
  3. Assign the appropriate privileged roles to the new accounts:
    • Navigate to the user profile > Assigned roles
    • Select + Add assignments and choose the necessary roles
  4. Once cloud-only accounts are fully operational, remove privileged role rights from the hybrid accounts:
    • Go to Identity > Roles and administrators
    • Select each role and remove the hybrid account assignments

Note: Maintain cloud-only accounts for all privileged roles. Protect them with strong authentication and regularly review their configuration and usage.

Indicators.Name: Privileged account with mailbox
Indicators.Description:
This indicator searches for privileged accounts in the Entra tenant that have an associated mailbox.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.All
  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • Directory.Read.All
  • MailboxSettings.Read
Indicators.Remediation:
Monitor the detected privileged users' mailboxes to ensure that they are not being used in a non-administrative way. In addition, use unified audit logs to investigate suspicious activity. Also regularly rotate passwords and avoid using default or easily guessable passwords. Furthermore, enforce strong password policies for administrative accounts and train administrators on security best practices, including identifying phishing attempts and avoiding suspicious links. Another important thing is to enable MFA for privileged accounts, to add an extra layer of security by requiring a second form of authentication.

To enable MFA for a user:

Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Authentication Administrator. Browse to Identity, select users and then All users. Click on Per-user MFA. Find the privileged user you want to enable for per-user Microsoft Entra multifactor authentication. You might need to change the view at the top to users. Then Check the box next to the name(s) of the user(s) to change the state for. On the right-hand side, under quick steps and choose Enable.

Indicators.Name: Privileged Identity Management group missing activation approval
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if any eligible scheduled assignments of Privileged Identity Management group roles, assigned to Entra privileged roles, do not require approval to activate.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.All
  • PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.Read.AzureADGroup
  • PrivilegedAccess.Read.AzureADGroup
  • Organization.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
It is recommended to enable the "Require approval to activate" setting for groups that are used for elevating into privileged roles. This ensures that role activation is controlled and requires approval from an administrator.

  1. Open the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Navigate to: Identity Governance > Privileged Identity Management > Groups.
  3. Select the relevant group.
  4. Under Settings, select the role you want to configure.
  5. Click Edit.
  6. Check the box for "Require approval to activate".
  7. Select the relevant approver(s).
  8. Click Update to save the changes.

Indicators.Name: Entra ID privileged user with privileges in AD
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for Entra ID privileged users that are also privileged in on-premise AD.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • RoleManagement.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Before revoking privileges from these accounts, review the identified users to fully understand their operational workflows. Check both Active Directory audit logs and Microsoft Entra sign-in logs to determine how and when they exercise their administrative privileges in each distinct environment.

Caution: Instantly revoking privileges in either directory may disrupt critical administrative tasks or unexpectedly lock out administrators attempting to manage hybrid infrastructure. Privilege separation must be carefully coordinated to ensure continuity of IT operations.

To safely separate privileges, the recommended approach is to create a dedicated, cloud-only account exclusively for Microsoft Entra ID administration, and subsequently remove the cloud privileges from the synchronized on-premises account. To execute this separation:

  1. Navigate to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Expand Identity, expand Users, and select All users.
  3. Select New user and create a dedicated, cloud-only account for Microsoft Entra administration. Do not synchronize this account from Active Directory.
  4. Expand Roles & admins, select Roles & admins, and assign the necessary privileged roles strictly to this new cloud-only account.
  5. Navigate back to All users, locate the original hybrid user account, and select it.
  6. In the left navigation menu, select Assigned roles. Select the checkboxes next to the highly privileged roles, and select Remove assignment to revoke their cloud privileges.

Indicators.Name: AD privileged user synced to Entra ID
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for AD privileged users that are synced to Entra ID.

Required permissions

  • User.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the users identified as holding privileges in Active Directory, and remove them from synchronization in Entra Connect or Entra cloud sync.

In Entra Connect, user filtering should be configured on an Organizational unit level. This requires modification of the filtering on the Entra Connect server, as well as any staging servers. Details on adjusting the OU filtering can be found in the reference Microsoft documentation.

In Entra cloud sync, user filtering is configured with scoping filters. Details on adjusting scoping filters can be found in the reference Microsoft documentation.

Organizations must ensure that changes to synchronized users are understood and verified that they will not negatively impact the target users, and any impacted users should have the changes communicated as needed.

Indicators.Name: Prohibited Entra ID role assigned
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for the assignment of roles in Entra ID that are deprecated or prohibited from use.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • RoleManagement.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review all principals with prohibited role assignments and remove these assignments immediately.

To review and manage role assignments, open the Microsoft Entra admin center, go to Identity > Roles and admins.

For each prohibited role:

  1. Identify alternative, supported roles that provide the necessary permissions.
  2. Remove the prohibited role assignment.
  3. Assign the appropriate alternative role.
  4. Verify that the principal can still perform their required tasks with the new role assignment.

For deprecated roles, consult Microsoft documentation to find the recommended replacement roles.

For "prohibited" roles, revoke all assignments and reassess the need for those permissions.

Deprecated roles: PowerShell fallback

Deprecated roles are sometimes not visible or manageable through the Entra admin center UI. In those cases, use the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK to locate and remove the assignment directly via the underlying Graph API.

Step 1 - List the role assignments for the affected principal (use the principal's Object ID from the indicator results):

Get-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignment -Filter "PrincipalId eq '<ObjectId>'"

This returns a list of assignment records. Note the Id (the assignment ID) and the RoleDefinitionId for each assignment you want to investigate.

Step 2 - Confirm the role name before removing it:

Get-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleDefinition -UnifiedRoleDefinitionId <RoleDefinitionId>

Verify the DisplayName matches the deprecated/prohibited role you intend to remove. Do not skip this step.

Step 3 - Remove the assignment:

Remove-MgRoleManagementDirectoryRoleAssignment -UnifiedRoleAssignmentId <AssignmentId>

Repeat Steps 1-3 for each affected principal. Re-run Step 1 after removal to confirm the assignment is gone.

Note: The cmdlets above are part of the Microsoft.Graph PowerShell module. Cmdlet names and parameters may change across module versions. Always verify against the installed module's documentation (Get-Help <cmdlet>) before running in production.

Caution: Ensure that removing these role assignments does not disrupt critical operations. Always test changes in a non-production environment first.

Indicators.Name: AZUREADSSOACC account with resource-based constrained delegation
Indicators.Description: This indicator looks for Resource-based constrained delegation (RBCD) configured on the Entra Seamless SSO account.
Indicators.Remediation:
Clear the msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity attribute on the AZUREADSSOACC computer account.

There is no functional reason to allow resource-based constrained delegation on this computer account.


To remove, run the following PowerShell command against the computer account:


Set-ADComputer -Identity AZUREADSSOACC$ -Clear "msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity"

Organizations should also investigate the necessity for Entra Seamless SSO. If devices are configured for hybrid join, Seamless SSO is not used. Refer to the reference Microsoft article for more information about SSO with a primary refresh token (PRT) vs. the Seamless SSO system.

Indicators.Name: Report suspicious MFA activity disabled
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if the setting to report suspicious MFA activity is enabled.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
  • GroupMember.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
It is recommended to have the "Report suspicious activity" setting enabled for all users. Please note that if you are using the "Microsoft managed" option, the "Report suspicious activity" setting will be disabled.

To configure the "Report suspicious activity" setting, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), browse to Protection > Authentication methods > Settings > Report suspicious activity, and confirm that State is set to Enabled and Target is All users.

Indicators.Name: MFA required for Entra device registration and join
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether Microsoft Entra's Device Registration or Conditional Access policies enforce MFA for device registration and join operations.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
To ensure secure onboarding of devices into your Microsoft Entra environment, you should enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) during the device registration process. This can be accomplished in one or both of the following ways:

  1. Configure the Device Registration Policy: Navigate to the Microsoft Entra admin center and go to Identity > Devices > Device settings. Locate the Device registration section and enable the option that requires MFA to join devices to Azure AD. This setting enforces MFA across the entire tenant when users register or join devices.
  2. Create or Modify a Conditional Access Policy: Go to Microsoft Entra admin center > Identity > Conditional Access. Create a new policy or update an existing one that targets the user population involved in device join:
    • Under Users, choose "All users".
    • Under Target Resources > User Actions, choose "Register or join devices"
    • Under Access controls > Grant > Grant Access, choose "Require multifactor authentication" or "Require authentication strength"
    Microsoft recommends using "Authentication Strength", as it's choosing a fine-grained, specific type of MFA.

After implementing these changes, users will be prompted for MFA when registering devices, helping to prevent unauthorized device enrollment and align your environment with Zero Trust best practices.

Indicators.Name: Conditional Access policy does not require MFA on privileged accounts
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether Conditional Access policies require mutli-factor authentication (MFA) for privileged accounts.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Users identified as impacted must have a Conditional Access policy applied that enforces MFA.

Break-glass accounts may be an exception to MFA requirements and can be added to an ignore list for this indicator. Organizations need to monitor their break-glass accounts to ensure that the accounts are not used without awareness.

Microsoft provides both a Conditional Access policy template, as well as step-by-step instructions for creating a Conditional Access Policy requiring MFA for administrators.

If a Conditional Access policy already exists for privileged users, the identified users or roles can be added to that policy instead.

The policy implemented should implement MFA for the following roles:

Agent ID Administrator, AI Administrator, AI Reader, Application Administrator, Application Developer, Attribute Provisioning Administrator, Attribute Provisioning Reader, Authentication Administrator, Authentication Extensibility Administrator, Authentication Extensibility Password Administrator, Authentication Policy Administrator, B2C IEF Keyset Administrator, Billing Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator, Cloud Device Administrator, Conditional Access Administrator, Directory Synchronization Accounts, Directory Writers, Domain Name Administrator, Exchange Administrator, External Identity Provider Administrator, Global Administrator, Global Reader, Helpdesk Administrator, Hybrid Identity Administrator, Identity Governance Administrator, Intune Administrator, Lifecycle Workflows Administrator, Partner Tier1 Support, Partner Tier2 Support, Password Administrator, Privileged Authentication Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator, Security Administrator, Security Operator, Security Reader, SharePoint Administrator, User Administrator.

Additional privileged roles can be added if desired.

Implementing changes to Conditional Access policies and enabling security defaults can both negatively impact users if not properly tested. Organizations need to verify all policy and security changes and communicate them accordingly.

Indicators.Name: Conditional Access policy does not require MFA when sign-in risk identified
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether a Conditional Access policy exists that requires MFA if the authentication request risk is medium or high as determined by Entra ID Protection.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
  • Organization.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Deploy a Conditional Access policy requiring MFA for risky sign-ins.

Microsoft provides both a Conditional Access policy template, as well as step-by-step instructions for creating a Conditional Access Policy requiring MFA for risky sign-ins.

Implementing changes to Conditional Access policies can negatively impact users if not properly tested. Organizations need to verify all policy and security changes and communicate them out accordingly.

Indicators.Name: Conditional Access policy does not require a password change for high risk users
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether a conditional access policy exists that requires a password change for users marked as high-risk by Entra ID Protection.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
  • Organization.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Deploy a Conditional Access policy requiring password change for high-risk users.

Microsoft provides both a Conditional Access policy template, as well as step-by-step instructions for creating a Conditional Access Policy requiring password change for high-risk users.

Implementing changes to Conditional Access policies can negatively impact users if not properly tested. Organizations need to verify all policy and security changes and communicate them out accordingly.

Indicators.Name: Restricted administrative unit
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for administrative units that are part of the tenant and have restricted management enabled. This configuration can allow attackers to "lock in" malicious accounts so that only scoped administrators can remove them, potentially delaying remediation and prolonging unauthorized access.

Required permissions

  • AdministrativeUnit.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Organizations should regularly audit their restricted administrative units (AUs) in Entra ID to ensure they are configured intentionally and securely. Begin by reviewing all existing restricted AUs and confirming their purpose, assigned administrators, and member objects.

Verify that only authorized and trusted accounts have administrative roles scoped to each AU. Remove any unnecessary role assignments. If an AU no longer requires restricted management, consider removing it, depending on operational needs. Note that once created, an administrative unit cannot be converted back to an unrestricted state.

  1. To review restricted administrative units, open the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Expand Roles & admins.
  3. Select Admin units.
  4. Using the "Add filters" option, choose "Restricted management" and select "Yes" to see only restricted AUs.
  5. Review each AU by clicking on it.

Indicators.Name: Entra custom role with risky permission
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if a custom role contains risky permissions

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the permissions assigned to the custom role.

Organizations should determine if risky permissions cna be removed from the role. If not, use of the role should be limited as needed.

To review and manage role assignments, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, select Show more, expand Roles & admins, and select Roles & admins.

In the blade on the right, find the custom role. Select the role. A new blade will open with the role settings. Under Manage in this blade, select Description.

From this view you can review role permissions. To remove permissions, select Edit.

Indicators.Name: Risky users (medium or high level)
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for risky users in the tenant with medium or high level of risk.

Required permissions

  • IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All
  • Organization.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation: Remediating risky users in enterprise identity (Entra ID) systems involves implementing a multi-faceted approach that includes comprehensive risk assessment, user education and training on security best practices, enforcement of strong authentication measures such as multi-factor authentication, regular review and adjustment of user access privileges to adhere to the principle of least privilege, continuous monitoring and anomaly detection for early identification of suspicious activities, establishment of an effective incident response plan for prompt containment and remediation of security incidents, and collaboration with security partners and regulatory bodies to stay abreast of emerging threats and best practices. By implementing these measures, organizations can mitigate the risks associated with risky users and enhance the overall security posture of their Entra ID systems.

Indicators.Name: User with security questions enabled
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if security questions are enabled for Entra self-service password reset.

Required permissions

  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Consider deprecating security questions as method available for self-service password reset.

If the organization does not have a policy around the use of knowledge-based authentication (KBA), known as security questions in Entra ID, NIST indicates in SP 800-63B, under section 5.1.1.2, that providers should not use KBA.

To review the existing security question settings, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Protection, select Password reset.

In the blade on the right, select Authentication methods. You can review the settings for the number of security questions required for reset, as well as view the questions available under Select security questions.

Indicators.Name: Service principal assigned as privileged group owner
Indicators.Description:
This indicator detects when a service principal (non-human identity) is assigned as an owner of a group with privileged roles. This configuration poses a potential security risk.

Required Permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • Directory.Read.All
  • GroupMember.Read.All
  • Application.Read.All
  • PrivilegedEligibilitySchedule.Read.AzureADGroup
Indicators.Remediation:
Review all service principals assigned as owners of privileged groups and assess whether this ownership is necessary. Where possible, remove ownership and replace with human administrator accounts.

For PIM-managed groups:

  1. Open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link).
  2. Navigate to Privileged Identity Management.
  3. Select the relevant privileged group, expand Roles, and go to Owner.
  4. Review the list of owners and remove service principals as needed.

For directly assigned (non-PIM) groups:

  1. Open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link).
  2. Navigate to All groups.
  3. Select the relevant role-assignable group and go to Owners.
  4. Review the list of owners and remove service principals as needed.

Apply the principle of least privilege for service principals and regularly audit application permissions.

Indicators.Name: AZUREADSSOACC account with password last set over 90 days ago
Indicators.Description: This indicator checks the Entra Seamless Single Sign-On computer account, AZUREADSSOACC, to determine if the password has been rotated in the last 90 days.
Indicators.Remediation:
The Kerberos decryption key used for Entra Seamless Single Sign-On must be rolled.


For details on the process of rolling the key, refer to the Microsoft reference article.

Organizations should also investigate the necessity for Entra Seamless SSO. If devices are configured for hybrid join, Seamless SSO is not used. Refer to the reference Microsoft article for more information about SSO with a primary refresh token (PRT) vs. the Seamless SSO system.

Indicators.Name: Self-service password reset enabled for privileged roles
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks whether users in privileged roles in Entra ID can use self-service password reset.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Disable SSPR for privileged roles.

To disable SSPR for privileged roles, you cannot use the Entra admin center. Organizations must use either the Microsoft Graph API or the Microsoft Graph PowerShell SDK to disable SSPR for privileged roles. See the reference articles for details on how to disable. The policy setting AllowedToUseSSPR should be set to false.

Organizations must ensure that disabling SSPR for privileged roles does not negatively impact their ability to administer their Entra tenant, and should ensure their break-glass accounts are working and maintained prior to disabling.

Indicators.Name: Guest invites not accepted in last 30 days
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for guest invites that were not redeemed within 30 days of the invitation.

Required permissions

  • User.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Guest accounts that have not accepted their invitation should be evaluated for cleanup.

Guest users can server multiple purposes in an Entra tenant for an organization. If guest users have never redeemed their invitation, then the intended access to the resources they have been assigned permissions has never been used, and may result in excessive unnecessary permissions.

Guest users though may be created for legitimate reasons in an Entra tenant, including:

  • Membership in an Office 365 group
  • Membership in an Exchange Online distribution list
  • Membership in a Teams channel for email
  • Guest accounts being used as contact objects

Organizations must review the legitimacy of why the guest users exist in the tenant, and make a decision on how to clean up or keep the accounts.

Indicators.Name: Suspicious Directory Synchronization Accounts role member
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for objects assigned the Directory Synchronization Accounts role that are not the default Entra Connect users.

Required permissions

  • Directory.Read.All
  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • AuditLog.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Remove the objects from the Directory Synchronization Accounts role assignment.

Role management for Directory Synchronization Accounts cannot be performed from the Entra admin center.

Organizations are responsible for verification of all changes they make to this role. Removal of a Entra connect account from this role may break directory synchronization processes.

There are different methods for connecting to Microsoft Graph to perform operations on this role assignment. These steps us Graph Explorer.

To verify role membership, open Graph Explorer (direct link).

Sign in to the impacted tenant on the right-hand side by selecting the user icon. By default Graph Explorer shows a set of sample tenant data.

Perform a GET against the beta API with the following query:

https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/directoryRoles(roleTemplateId='{{d29b2b05-8046-44ba-8758-1e26182fcf32}}')/members

In the response preview pane, the membership of the Directory Synchronization Accounts role is displayed.

Follow the instructions for Remove member documented here by Microsoft to remove the abnormal user:

Remove directory role member - Microsoft Graph beta | Microsoft Learn

Indicators.Name: Unprivileged owner of a privileged group
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for the presence of an unprivileged owner of a group with privileged roles.

Required permissions

  • RoleManagement.Read.Directory
  • Directory.Read.All
  • GroupMember.Read.All
  • RoleAssignmentSchedule.Read.Directory
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the principals assigned the ownership of a given privileged group, and determine if the ownership can be removed.

To review and manage role assignments, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Privileged Identity Management, select the privileged group name, expand Roles under the Manage blade, and select Owner.

Select each unprivileged principal and consider its ownership.

From this view you can remove principals as necessary from the group's ownership.

Organizations must ensure that any removal of the unprivileged owners does not impact the ability to manage their Entra tenant.

Indicators.Name: User not using their privileged role
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for users who have not activated a role assigned to them for over 30 days.

For users eligible via group membership, audit log retention in Entra ID may prevent gathering an accurate 'EligibleSince' date.

Required permissions

  • RoleEligibilitySchedule.Read.Directory
  • GroupMember.Read.All
  • Directory.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Review the users identified and the unused roles they hold, and determine if they should continue to hold these unused roles. A privileged access strategy should follow a governance plan for assigning least privilege, such as that documented in NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5.

You can review existing role assignments in the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link).

Organizations should use the Access Reviews feature of Entra Privileged Identity Management to help manage the lifecycle of privileged role assignments.

Indicators.Name: Users can create security groups
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if non-admin users can create security groups.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Disable Users can create security groups in the Entra tenant.

To disable, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Identity, expand Users, and select User settings.

In the blade on the right, toggle Users can create security groups to no.

Select Save at the bottom of the blade.

Organizations should understand how this change impacts their users and communicate the change out according to defined business processes.

Indicators.Name: Non-admin users can create tenants
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks if non-admin users are allowed to create Entra tenants.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enable Restrict non-admin users from creating tenants in the Entra tenant.

To enable, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Entra ID, expand Users, and select User settings.

In the blade on the right, toggle Restrict non-admin users from creating tenants to yes.

Select Save at the bottom of the blade.

Organizations should understand how this change impacts their users and communicate the change out according to defined business processes.

Indicators.Name: Non-admin users can register custom applications
Indicators.Description:
This indicator checks for an authorization policy that allows non-admin users to register applications in your Entra tenant.

Required permissions

  • Policy.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Disable Users can register applications in the Entra tenant.

To disable, open the Microsoft Entra admin center (direct link), expand Entra ID, expand Users, and select User settings.

In the blade on the right, toggle Users can register applications to no.

Select Save at the bottom of the blade.

Organizations should understand how this change impacts their users and communicate the change out according to defined business processes.

Indicators.Name: Non-privileged user cannot complete MFA
Indicators.Description:
Indicates whether non-privileged users in the tenant can use and complete the MFA process based on the authentication details that the user entered.

Required permissions

  • AuditLog.Read.All
  • User.Read.All
Indicators.Remediation:
Enforce MFA authentication for users in the tenant by Conditional Access Policies. In case no Premium P1/P2 licenses are used, enable Security Defaults in Entra ID.

To Create MFA access condition policy:

Browse to Protection, Conditional Access and then Policies. Select New policy. Give your policy a name. Under Assignments, select Users or workload identities. Under Include, select All users. Under Exclude select Users and groups and choose your organization's emergency access or break-glass accounts. Under Target resources, Resources (formerly cloud apps) and under Include, select All resources (formerly 'All cloud apps'). Under Exclude, select any applications that don't require multifactor authentication. Under Access controls, click on Grant, select Grant access. Select "Require authentication strength", then select the built-in "Multifactor authentication strength" from the list. Select Select. Select Create to create to enable your policy.

To enable Security Defaults:

Browse to Identity and then Overview and Properties. Select Manage security defaults. Set Security defaults to Enabled. Select Save.

Indicators.Name: Abnormal password refresh
Indicators.Description:
This indicator detects user accounts where the password change timestamp (pwdLastSet) does not match the underlying attribute metadata (unicodePwd change record).
This mismatch suggests the password may have been modified in a way that bypasses normal Active Directory update behavior or replication consistency.
